title: Polymorphic mapper and idempotency protocol for OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers using Redwood with clients built for the OpenAI Chat Completions API report edge-case mismatches when (a) streaming partial SSE/event chunks, (b) invoking function_call semantics, and (c) expecting structured outputs and idempotent retries. Our current compatibility shim covers 80% of traffic but fails on several practical cases: streamed partial function call payloads, messages with polymorphic role labels, missing 'finish_reason' semantics, and clients that rely on OpenAI-style idempotency via a request token.

Proposal: Implement a polymorphic request/response mapper that translates OpenAI Chat Completions (OA-CC) requests into Redwood internal canonical RPCs and maps responses back with deterministic rules. Add an explicit idempotency protocol layer to accept an OpenAI-style client idempotency token header, persist minimal request fingerprint metadata, and reconcile retries for streaming and non-streaming requests. Provide thorough test harnesses for streaming function_call flows and structured output validation.
acceptance_criteria: OA-CC messages with role variants (assistant/system/user/custom) correctly map to Redwood canonical roles without loss of provenance
Streaming SSE output to OA-CC clients preserves token-level partials, function_call start/continue/end frames, and maps finish_reason semantics consistently
Function calling: requests with function definitions are routed to our function call execution path; returned structured arguments are encoded into OA-CC tool_call events matching client expectations
Idempotency: client-supplied idempotency token prevents duplicate execution for retried requests within 10 minutes, with clear telemetry for dedup events
Backward-compatible: existing Redwood SDK customers unaffected; compatibility layer behind flag or compatibility-mode config
Automated test suite with >=50 unit + integration scenarios covering chunked streaming, network reconnects, and mixed function_call/assistant content
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests. 2) Canary behind compatibility-mode flag for 5% of OA-CC traffic in staging. 3) Monitor dedup, latency, and error rates for 48h. 4) Ramp to 25% then 100% if no regressions. 5) Post-mortem + docs update.
testing_plan: Create a harness that simulates OpenAI client behavior: normal requests, aborted streams, retried idempotent requests, function calls that produce multi-frame JSON args, and malformed role labels. Tests: unit mapping rules, integration against streaming server (local runtime), end-to-end QA with a test client. Include fuzz test for role/metadata polymorphism.
notes: Key trade-offs discussed: 1) Keep mapping pure stateless transformer vs persist sidecar state for streaming reassembly. We chose a lightweight persisted fingerprint store (Redis with 10m TTL) to support safe dedup without large storage costs. 2) Preserve OpenAI wire semantics for finish_reason and delta fragments even if our runtime emits different internal event shapes — we will canonicalize on the outbound path.
implementation_todo: Define canonical mapping table for message.role -> internal.role
Implement streaming frame reassembler to convert runtime chunks into OA-CC SSE chunks with delta/role/finish_reason fields
Add idempotency header parser and fingerprint persistence with configurable TTL
Wire function_call argument streaming: ensure partial JSON fragments are reassembled and validated before emitting 'tool_call' completion to OA-CC client
Add comprehensive unit + integration tests and a compatibility-mode feature flag
Update SDK adapters and docs to expose compatibility-mode toggle
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Persistent dedup store could become a scaling bottleneck under massive burst traffic. Mitigation: use sharded Redis cluster and sample-based bloom filter to short-circuit obvious duplicates.
Risk: Mis-mapped roles break customer business logic relying on role provenance. Mitigation: keep original role metadata in 'x-original-role' field in telemetry and optional passthrough header.
Risk: Partial JSON reassembly bugs cause silent function_call failures. Mitigation: strict schema validation + fallback to original raw payload saved in debug-store for replay
